subject: Claripay — first-packet performance & streaming plan
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@claripay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Claripay — first-packet performance & streaming plan

Thanks for the call this morning, Maria — good to meet the Claripay engineering team. Short recap and a few asks so we can lock the pilot config: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Target experience: payments flows with short prompts (10-60 tokens) and occasional long-form reconciliation (1k+ tokens).
- Peak shapes: you said most traffic is spiky around batch settlement windows, with steady-state during business hours.
- Mobile clients matter — your SDKs need predictable first-response times.

Performance asks / proposals for pilot:
1) Time-to-first-packet target: can you confirm an acceptable first-packet (first non-empty chunk) SLA? We suggested aiming for 200–250 ms P50 at pilot scale for interactive paths, with 95th under 500 ms.
2) Throughput & concurrency: please share expected RPS and peak concurrency for early pilot (we estimate 50–150 RPS based on the call; please correct).
3) Streaming: we recommend starting with Server-Sent Events (SSE) for the web dashboard and a WebSocket option for mobile SDKs. Need to confirm which you want to prioritize.
4) Chunk cadence: propose either time-based (every ~200 ms) or token-based (every ~128–256-token chunk). For short prompts time-based smaller packets (100–250 ms) reduce perceived latency.

Next steps I need from you to finalize the pilot plan (can take <24 hours):
- A short traffic sample (QPS by hour, typical sequence length distribution) — CSV is fine.
- Clarify the strict TTFT SLA for interactive flows (numeric P50/P95 targets).
- Whether WebSocket or SSE should be the primary streaming path for pilot.
- Security contact for SOC2/pen-test intake (we can share an evidence bundle once we confirm scope).

Attachments: claripay-integration-checklist.pdf (stub)

Proposed immediate milestone: internal pilot (technical validation) next week where we run synthetic traffic against a dedicated pool and measure first-packet and chunk sizes. If that looks good, we move to a small real-traffic beta.

Thanks — I can jump on a quick follow-up if helpful.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[jonas.weber@redwood.ai]
[attachment: claripay-integration-checklist.pdf]

From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@claripay.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Security Team <security@claripay.com>
Date: 2026-03-16T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Claripay — first-packet performance & streaming plan

Thanks, Jonas — great summary. Confirming items from our side and adding a few clarifications: 

Quick answers:
- Traffic sample: attaching an anonymized hourly QPS export for the last 30 days. Typical business-hour steady-state is ~40–80 RPS; peaks during batch windows hit ~180–220 RPS for a few minutes. (see claripay-traffic.csv)
- TTFT expectations: product team would like first visible token under 250 ms P50 for checkout flows, P95 under 600 ms is acceptable for now. For reconciliation UI slower is OK.
- Streaming preference: our mobile team prefers WebSocket for persistent sessions; web dashboard can use SSE. Prioritize WebSocket for the pilot.
- Sequence lengths: most user prompts are <120 tokens; reconciliation requests vary 1k–5k tokens.

Security: looping in security@claripay.com for SOC2 intake — they can confirm specific evidence fields.

We’re happy to run the pilot with the parameters you propose. Two asks from Claripay to Redwood:
- Can you provide the instrumentation events we should surface from the SDK (e.g., t_request_sent, t_first_chunk_received, chunk_count)?
- Pilot rollback plan if CPU/GPU utilization spikes during the peak burst window.

— Maria
Maria Gomez
Head of Product, Claripay
[attachment: claripay-traffic.csv]

On Tue, Mar 16, 2026 at 09:12 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for the call this morning, Maria — good to meet the Claripay engineering team...

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@claripay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Security Team <security@claripay.com>
Date: 2026-03-16T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Claripay — first-packet performance & streaming plan

Thanks for the fast turnaround, Maria — the traffic sample is very helpful. Quick replies to your asks and a proposed pilot config: 

Instrumentation events we will surface (SDK + server traces):
- request.sent_ts
- first_chunk.received_ts
- final_token.received_ts
- chunk.count
- chunk.bytes
- model.variant
- socket.connect_latency_ms

Pilot proposal (technical validation):
- Duration: 48 hours internal run, followed by 72 hours small beta with production routing
- Scale: synthetic ramp to 250 RPS to validate burst behavior (you said peaks to ~220 RPS)
- Concurrency target: model endpoints sized to handle sustained concurrency equivalent to 160 concurrent inflight requests
- First-packet target we’ll tune to P50 <= 220 ms, P95 <= 550 ms for interactive checkout flows.
- Streaming: default to WebSocket for the pilot; we'll include an SSE fallback for the dashboard.
- Chunk cadence: start with time-based cadence at 150–220 ms for short prompts; allow token-based for long-form outputs (256-token flush).
- Fallbacks: automatic model-variant fallback to a smaller quantized footprint if queueing exceeds target thresholds.

Pilot instrumentation & SLIs we’ll measure:
- time_to_first_chunk (P50/P95)
- end_to_end_latency (token stream completion)
- error_rate (5xx and application errors)
- cpu/gpu_utilization and queuing depth

Rollback/runbook: we will provide a step-by-step with thresholds and actions (scale, throttle, fallback). Draft attached as pilot-runbook.md (stub). Aditya will own the run and provide a live dashboard during the run.

Next concrete steps: 
1) Claripay to confirm WebSocket as pilot primary and sign off on the proposed SLO numbers above.
2) Claripay to share security contact’s list of required evidence items so we can prep SOC2 bundle.
3) Redwood to schedule an internal dry run on Thursday and share the runbook and dashboard link.

I’ll schedule a 30-minute kickoff with Aditya and your engineering lead — propose Thursday 10:00 AM PT unless that conflicts.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: pilot-runbook.md]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@claripay.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Security Team <security@claripay.com>
Date: 2026-03-16T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Claripay — first-packet performance & streaming plan

Quick technical notes from engineering side — will join the kickoff: 

Pilot config specifics (ops-friendly):
- Model: rwd-instruct-3b-quant (balanced latency/cost). We’ll bring a smaller rwd-chat-1.4b-quant for auto-fallback.
- Reserved concurrency for pilot endpoints: start at 32 per shard, scaleable with autoscaler (limits set to prevent noisy neighbor issues).
- Batching: start with micro-batching disabled for interactive checkout paths (to minimize TTFT); enable single-request batching for long-form reconciliation.
- Socket defaults: WebSocket keepalive 45s, ping interval 20s, idle close 2m.
- Chunking implementation: server emits at most 1 chunk per 120–220 ms for short prompts; allow 1s flush for very large outputs to reduce fragmentation.

Instrumentation we’ll expose in the test harness (SDK + tracing):
- event.request_sent (trace_id)
- event.chunk_first_received (trace_id, bytes)
- event.chunk_stream_complete
- metric.queue_depth
- metric.gpu_utilization_pct

On rollback: 
- If queue_depth > 12 for >30s at pilot scale, we will trigger: increase model shards (if capacity), enable fallback variant, or enable throttling on non-critical routes.

I’ll bring a dashboard with the above SLOs to the kickoff. Happy to adjust the numbers after we see the dry-run traces.

— Aditya Rao
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
